prompt: What does `probe` print when it measures a page?
hint: It asks the browser the questions DevTools answers.

choices.text: What Chromium reports about the page
choices.why: Right. Boxes, computed values, the accessibility tree: the answers a browser gave, printed as text.

choices.text: The numbers the author expected the page to have
choices.why: The opposite: it exists so the lessons quote what a browser printed instead of what somebody expected.

choices.text: A score for how good the page's design is
choices.why: Nothing in the course grades a design. probe reports facts about what was drawn.

choices.text: A screenshot of the page saved as a picture
choices.why: A picture is exactly what is hard to quote. probe prints text you can compare.

prompt: Why are this course's questions about predicting what the browser will do?
hint: Think about what can be checked mechanically.

choices.text: Because building pages is not part of the course
choices.why: Building is the practice, done in your own browser. The questions check the other half.

choices.text: Predicting is easier than writing, so it suits a first course
choices.why: Predicting is the harder half: it is what separates writing CSS on purpose from trying until it looks right.

choices.text: A rendered page has no answer key, and a prediction does
choices.why: Right. Nothing here can look at your page and judge it, but a width or a winning rule has one right answer.

choices.text: Browsers disagree, so only Chromium's answer counts
choices.why: The course measures with Chromium for reproducibility, not because other engines are wrong.

prompt: Where can you read, by hand, the same numbers `probe` prints for an element?

choices.text: In the page's HTML source
choices.why: The source is what was sent. Sizes and computed colours exist only after the browser lays the page out.

choices.text: In the Network panel, beside each file
choices.why: Network lists requests and timings. Boxes and computed values are in Elements.

choices.text: In the stylesheet the page links to
choices.why: The stylesheet says what was asked for. Which rule won, and the size that came out, are only in the browser.

choices.text: DevTools' Elements panel, in Computed
choices.why: Right. Click the element, and the Computed tab and box diagram show what probe prints.

choices.text: Your own computer, as it is

choices.text: A server rented for the course

choices.why: The server sends text. Size is decided in the browser, by CSS.

choices.text: The `<h1>` tag itself, which means 'large text'

choices.text: The font installed on the reader's computer

prompt: A heading is drawn with a `<div>` styled big and bold. Who loses something?
hint: Three readers never look at the picture.

choices.text: The author, who has to write more CSS
choices.why: Possibly, but that is a cost to the author. The readers who lose are the ones who cannot see the styling.

choices.text: Nobody: it looks exactly like a heading
choices.why: It looks like one to a sighted reader. To a screen reader and a search engine it is one more block of text.

choices.text: Screen reader users and search engines
choices.why: Right. Both find headings only in the HTML, and a styled div is not one.

choices.text: Only the browser, which draws it more slowly
choices.why: Speed is not the problem. Meaning is: nothing tells any program this is a heading.

prompt: Why do browsers repair broken HTML instead of refusing it?

choices.text: Repairing a page is faster for the browser than drawing an error page
choices.why: Speed was never the reason. Users preferred the browser that showed the page.

choices.text: Users picked whichever one displayed the page
choices.why: Right. Showing something for any input won, and the HTML standard now defines the repairs.

choices.text: Broken HTML was invalid in old versions of the language and is accepted now
choices.why: It is invalid in every version. Browsers repair it anyway.

choices.text: The server fixes it before sending
choices.why: Servers send the bytes they have. The repair happens in the browser's parser.

choices.why: The browser does not drop it. Presence is the information.

choices.text: Yes: the attribute is present, and that is all it checks
choices.why: Right. A boolean attribute is on when present, whatever its value says. To turn it off, remove it.

choices.text: It depends on the browser
choices.why: The standard is exact here, and every browser follows it: present means on.

choices.text: No: the value false turns it off
choices.why: That is how it would work in a programming language. In HTML the value of a boolean attribute is ignored.

choices.text: `<script>`

choices.why: No margin was set. The space belongs to the line, not to the image.

prompt: A page starts with `<html lang="en">` and no doctype. What does the browser do?

choices.why: There is no warning at all, which is the danger.

choices.text: Uses quirks mode

choices.text: Refuses to show it until a doctype is added

choices.why: Every page would share that cached file. Only one page is off.

choices.text: Whether the image files are the size the HTML says
choices.why: That would be wrong on every page using the image, not on one page only.

choices.text: Whether that page starts with the doctype, and so which mode it is in
choices.why: Right. One page in quirks mode follows different layout rules, silently, and compatMode or a validator says so.

choices.text: Whether the tutorial was written for a different browser
choices.why: The rule is right on every other page in the same browser.

choices.text: The author wrote that sentence in bold

choices.why: There is no error page. The text is drawn, damaged.

choices.text: The replacement character, �
choices.why: Right. The byte was not valid UTF-8, and the decoder wrote � where it made no sense.

choices.why: It trusted the declaration and did not detect anything.

choices.why: One guess on one file proves nothing about the next file or the next browser.

choices.why: Right. Another browser, another file or a server header can guess differently, so declare UTF-8.

choices.text: The file must have been saved in ISO-8859-1
choices.why: It was saved in UTF-8. Only latin1.html was re-encoded.

choices.text: Chromium reads files as UTF-8 when they declare no encoding
choices.why: It detected the encoding from the bytes. Detection is a guess, not a default.

choices.text: It makes the page slower to draw

choices.text: It stops people who need bigger text from zooming to read it

choices.why: Right. So stylesheets go early in the head, where the browser learns of them soonest.

choices.text: CSS has to run before HTML can be parsed
choices.why: Parsing continues during the download. Only drawing waits.
